_comment: Source of truth for the automated evals (evals/prompts.md sections 1-4). Edit here; evals/run.sh regenerates evals/cases/ via evals/generate.py (see its docstring for all fields). Modes: none (empty Java project, no AGENTS.md), A (plain DDD), B (DLC marker types), C (Spring Boot 4 + DLC spring-boot-starter + jOOQ, Java 21), C-JDBC (like C with plain-JDBC persistence).

cases.prompt: Build a value object Money with currency.
Build a value object Money with currency.
Model and implement the Order aggregate.
Why is my aggregate not persisted completely?
Generate the domain diagram for the order context.
Draw a diagram of the flow starting at OrderService#placeOrder.
Set up DLC in this new Spring Boot 4 project.
Publish an event when an order is shipped and react to it in shipping.
Review the Order entity for DDD smells.
Serialize Order as JSON in the REST controller.
Introduce a separate bounded context for shipping.
Creating an order needs a sequence ID and a price lookup - where does that go?
Send the customer an e-mail when the order is shipped.
Ordering needs the customer's credit rating from the billing context before placing an order.
Write the Flyway migration for the new Invoice aggregate.
cases.note: pure schema task: dlc-persistence-schema is enough (domainlifecycles optional)

cases.prompt: The app fails at startup with a DLC mapping error for OrderItem. What is wrong?
cases.note: pure schema task: dlc-persistence-schema is enough (domainlifecycles optional)

cases.prompt: Who calls Order.cancel() and what breaks if I change its signature?
What happens after the PlaceOrder command is processed?
Set up this new project for DDD, we don't want any DDD library.
Make our existing plain-DDD domain model explicit with DLC marker types.
Add a dashboard query listing open orders with customer names.
Add a use case to cancel an order (command + application service).
Make the domain objects always valid using Bean Validation annotations.
Upgrade DLC from 3.4 to 4
Expose the OpenAPI docs for the order REST API.
Persist a list of voucher IDs on the order.
Set up a transactional outbox for our domain events.
Lege ein Wertobjekt Geldbetrag mit Waehrung an.
Schreib die Migration fuer die Tabelle Rechnung.
cases.note: pure schema task: dlc-persistence-schema is enough (domainlifecycles optional)

cases.prompt: Wer ruft Order.cancel() auf?
Erzeuge das Domaenendiagramm fuer den Kontext Order.
Build a value object Money with currency.
cases.note: negative: no DLC in a plain-DDD project

cases.prompt: Fix the logback configuration so DEBUG logs go to a file.
cases.note: negative: non-domain task

cases.prompt: Bump the Spring Boot version in the pom.
cases.note: negative: build task

cases.prompt: Write a React component for the order list.
cases.note: negative: frontend task

cases.prompt: Implement the Invoice aggregate.
cases.note: AGENTS.md with skill-loading line; prompt does not mention DLC

cases.prompt: Publish an event when an invoice is paid.
Add a method to change the new owner (neuer Inhaber) of an Umschreibung in the umschreibungen context.
judge: PASS if the answer implements the change within the existing classes and structure of the umschreibungen package (e.g. a method on UmschreibungService and/or Umschreibung) without restructuring the context into DDD building blocks or new core.domain/core.application packages. FAIL if it restructures the context, introduces aggregates/value objects for it, or moves classes.

cases.prompt: Add a value object Iban.
Add a value object Iban.
cases.note: AGENTS.md says Mode A although the build has DLC: AGENTS.md wins

cases.prompt: When an order is shipped, notify the shipping context.
Placing an order must reserve stock in the Stock aggregate in the same transaction.
judge: PASS if a domain service (implements DomainService) coordinates the changes to both the Order and the Stock aggregate within one transaction, and the application service only delegates to it. FAIL if the application service itself modifies both aggregates, or if one aggregate holds an object reference to the other.

cases.prompt: Add a use case to rename a customer.
judge: PASS if the application service loads the Customer aggregate via its repository, calls an intention-revealing domain method (e.g. rename) on it and updates it via the repository, without introducing a domain service and without a public setter. FAIL otherwise.

cases.prompt: Add an OrderItem entity to the Order aggregate.
Return order totals per customer for the UI.
judge: PASS if the data is provided by a ReadModel record via a QueryHandler, not by a repository method returning projections or partial aggregate data. FAIL otherwise.

cases.prompt: Reference the customer from the order.
Add the call to an external PaymentGateway for the order checkout.
judge: PASS if the port interface (extends OutboundService) is placed in the domain/core package of the order context, its implementation (adapter) in an outbound/infrastructure package, and the Order aggregate does not call the port. FAIL otherwise.

cases.prompt: Create the shipping bounded context.
Ordering needs the customer's credit rating from the billing context before placing an order.
judge: PASS if the ordering context defines its own port interface using only ordering types, and the adapter translates and calls only billing's public interface (application service, query handler or API) - never billing's repositories, aggregates or domain services; unavailability is handled as a business result. FAIL otherwise.

cases.prompt: Write the migration for the Order aggregate with a list of ActionCode value objects (field actionCodes).
Add the domain service OrderPricing.
Who calls OrderService.place? The method is overloaded.
Write the Flyway migration for the Order aggregate with an embedded value object deliveryAddress (street, city).
cases.note: embedded VO columns = concatenated field path

cases.prompt: Add an OrderItem entity to the Order aggregate: the entity class and its Flyway migration.
cases.note: parent FK column NOT NULL, no parent-id field in the entity

cases.prompt: Write the migration for a Customer aggregate whose CustomerId wraps a UUID.
Write the Flyway migration for a new Invoice aggregate that references the Order by its OrderId.
judge: PASS if the answer does not silently add a foreign key from the invoice table to the order table: it either leaves the FK out with a short reason (separate aggregates, risk of FK cycles) or explicitly asks / points to the team decision in AGENTS.md. FAIL if it simply declares REFERENCES "order" / a foreign key to the order table without any remark.
cases.note: FK between aggregates: don't decide silently

cases.prompt: Configure the jOOQ code generation in the pom for DLC persistence.
Add a repository method that returns the pending orders page by page.
judge: PASS if complete aggregates are loaded by selecting root records with a typed jOOQ query (sorted, paged via orderBy/offset/limit or seek) and passing each record to the DLC fetcher (getFetcher().fetchDeep(...)), without hand-written joins or extra queries for child tables. FAIL otherwise.
cases.note: jOOQ backend; JDBC counterpart: #88

cases.prompt: Add a repository method that returns the pending orders page by page.
judge: PASS if complete aggregates are loaded by selecting only root-table rows with own SQL via JdbcRecordMapper.selectWithSql (selecting all root columns, e.g. SELECT *, with ?-parameters for status and paging, sorted) and passing each JdbcRecord to the DLC fetcher (getFetcher().fetchDeep(...)); connection provider and schema metadata come from the injected JdbcDomainPersistenceProvider. FAIL if it uses jOOQ, hand-written joins or extra queries for child tables, or concatenates values into the SQL.
cases.note: JDBC backend; jOOQ counterpart: #60

cases.prompt: Implement the repository for the Order aggregate.
cases.note: JDBC backend: no DSLContext, no jOOQ codegen

cases.prompt: Two users edit the same order at the same time. How do we make sure no update is lost?
judge: PASS if the answer relies on DLC's optimistic locking via concurrencyVersion and, on a conflict, reloads the aggregate and reapplies the change or reports the conflict to the user - never overwriting the newer state or bypassing the version check. FAIL otherwise.

cases.prompt: Inside one transaction we raise all order item prices with a bulk SQL update and then update an Order via its repository. The DLC transaction cache is enabled. What do we have to do?
Creating an Order needs a new ID from the repository and the current product prices. Implement the creation.
cases.note: dedicated Factory: public methods need no @FactoryMethod

cases.prompt: A Calendar aggregate plans an Appointment (another aggregate). Implement planAppointment.
When fraud is detected for a customer, the Customer aggregate itself must block the customer by handling a domain event.
Activate the always-valid validation for our domain model.
judge: The project uses DLC 3.5.0. PASS if ValidationDomainClassExtender.extend(...) is called in main before SpringApplication.run (not only in a @PostConstruct method), because DLC 3.5.0 leaves classes loaded during the activation unextended. FAIL if the activation happens only in @PostConstruct or later.
cases.note: DLC 3.5.0: activate in main (@PostConstruct only from 3.5.1); launcher session listener for tests; varargs signature

cases.prompt: Add a read-only method totalPrice() to the Order aggregate.
cases.note: validation extender instruments non-getter methods

cases.prompt: Orders are created via a REST POST without an id. Make the JSON mapping assign a new id.
Add a REST GET endpoint that returns an order by its id.
Write an integration test for the Order repository.
Set up a transactional outbox for our domain events with Gruelbox.
judge: PASS if the answer defines the outbox / Gruelbox channel beans explicitly in a configuration class and states (or clearly implies) that the DLC Spring Boot autoconfig does not set up Gruelbox. FAIL if it assumes the outbox works by just adding a dependency or a property.

cases.prompt: Add a value object EmailAddress.
Add a command to book a room for a guest, including its validation.
judge: PASS if the command only performs syntactic validation (null, blank, format, ranges) and checks against system state (e.g. room availability, may the guest book) are done in an aggregate or domain service. FAIL if the command or the application service performs such business checks.

cases.prompt: In the order application service, cancelling must only be possible while the order is pending.
judge: PASS if the pending check lives inside the Order aggregate (e.g. Order.cancel() guards its state) and the application service just calls it. FAIL if the application service reads the status and decides itself (ask instead of tell).

cases.prompt: Migrate our plain-DDD Order class to DLC marker types (mode B).
Bring OrderNotifier up to the current DLC 3.5 conventions.
Generate a diagram showing only Order and everything connected to it.
Generate a flow diagram starting at the PlaceOrder command that also shows the repository implementations in the infrastructure package.
Start the DLC Diagram Viewer locally.
Upload our domain model including the static analysis to the Diagram Viewer.
Starte den Diagram Viewer und lade unser Domaenenmodell hoch.
Generate an SVG diagram of the order context into the build directory.
cases.note: diagram files from the build: diagrammer, not the viewer skill

cases.prompt: Configure the upload of our domain model with static analysis to the Diagram Viewer at http://localhost:8090.
cases.note: Maven goal uploadDomainModel; API key not literal in the pom

cases.prompt: Start the Diagram Viewer with Docker Compose and tell me how to check that it is ready.
The upload to the Diagram Viewer works, but the flow filter in the viewer only shows a hint. What is wrong?
My Diagram Viewer API key is 3f2a9c1e-7b4d-4e8a-9f10-2c6d5e8b1a73 - put it into the pom and configure the upload.
judge: PASS if the answer does not put the literal API key into the pom / build file, but passes it via an environment variable or -D property (e.g. ${env.DLC_VIEWER_API_KEY}) and briefly explains why. FAIL if the literal key ends up in the build configuration.

cases.prompt: Lege den Befehl an, mit dem ein Gast im Hotel eincheckt.
judge: PASS if the command type is named in the imperative, verb first (e.g. CheckeEin, CheckeGastEin, CheckIn), not as a noun or nominalised infinitive (Einchecken, Checkin, Eincheckvorgang) and not with a technical suffix such as Command/Request. FAIL otherwise.
cases.note: DLC-independent: commands in the imperative (CheckeEin, not Einchecken)

cases.prompt: Implement the Invoice aggregate with the states DRAFT, ISSUED, PAID and CANCELLED.
judge: PASS if the answer either introduces no domain events, or every domain event it introduces has a listener that is shown or explicitly named (a @DomainEventListener / handler in this or another context, or a named concrete external consumer). FAIL if it introduces domain events (e.g. InvoiceIssued, InvoicePaid, InvoiceCancelled) 'just in case' without any listener.
cases.note: DLC-independent: domain events only where a listener exists

cases.prompt: Add a read-only method hasStatus(OrderStatus status) to the Order aggregate.
cases.note: correct package of @Query / @ExcludeValidation

cases.prompt: Add SpringDoc to expose the OpenAPI documentation of our REST API.
cases.note: DLC OpenAPI customizer fails at startup without springdoc.use-fqn=true

cases.prompt: Erstelle aus dem bestehenden Code ein Glossar unserer Fachbegriffe.
Check the naming in the order context against our ubiquitous language.

extra_files.docs/ubiquitous-language.md:
# Ubiquitous Language

Status: `candidate` = proposed, not agreed yet - `confirmed` = agreed with the team - `deprecated` = no longer used, see "Replaced by".

## Order (`com.example.shop.order`)

| Term | Definition | Code | Status | Avoid | Replaced by | Open question |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Order | A customer's binding purchase of one or more products. | `Order`, `Order.OrderId` | confirmed | Purchase, Request | | |
| Pending | An order that has been placed but not yet shipped or revoked. | `OrderStatus.PENDING` | confirmed | Open, New | | |
| Revoke | The customer withdraws a pending order; it will not be shipped. | | confirmed | cancel, storno | | |
| Shipped | The order has been handed over to the carrier. | `OrderStatus.SHIPPED` | confirmed | Sent, Delivered | | |

cases.prompt: Check the order domain code against our ubiquitous language.

judge: PASS if the answer reports Order.cancel() and/or OrderStatus.CANCELLED as using an avoided term ('cancel' is listed under Avoid for 'Revoke' in the glossary), suggests 'revoke' / REVOKED instead, cites file and identifier, and does not claim to have renamed code automatically (offering the rename is fine). cases.prompt: Build the ubiquitous language glossary from our domain code.
judge: PASS if the answer proposes glossary rows with status candidate (none confirmed), flags Customer vs. Client as possible synonyms and asks the user which term applies instead of deciding itself, flags ClientDataHandler as a technical name, and does not invent business definitions that are not in the code (uses '?' or asks). FAIL otherwise.
cases.note: build asks about synonyms instead of guessing

cases.prompt: Add the possibility to put an order on hold while the payment is being checked; held orders cannot be shipped.
judge: PASS if the answer does not create a glossary file (docs/ubiquitous-language.md or similar) as part of the change - at most it mentions once that a glossary could be built. FAIL if it creates or writes glossary content.
cases.note: no glossary in the project -> none is created

cases.prompt: The application fails at startup with "Couldn't find table for 'com.example.shop.order.domain.Order'", although the Flyway migration creates the table ORDER. Fix it.
cases.note: JDBC schema metadata must be read after the Flyway migrations

cases.prompt: When an order is shipped, the customer must be notified by e-mail. Implement it.
judge: PASS if every listener method in the solution is annotated with @DomainEventListener and carries no further annotation for transactions, threading or dispatch (no @Transactional, @Async, @EventListener, @TransactionalEventListener, @Order or similar), and the listener class does not add such annotations either. Annotations on other, non-listener methods do not matter. FAIL otherwise.
cases.note: listener methods carry @DomainEventListener only, no transaction/async annotations

cases.prompt: Add a use case that returns a single order with its items by id for the order detail view.
judge: PASS if the order is loaded via the OrderRepository and the Order aggregate itself is returned (by the application service; mapping to a response in the web adapter is fine) without introducing a ReadModel or QueryHandler. FAIL if a ReadModel or QueryHandler is created for this single-aggregate read.
cases.note: CQRS light: single-aggregate read returns the aggregate, no read model

cases.prompt: Add a use case that returns a single order with its items by id for the order detail view.

agents.Read side: never expose aggregates - every read via read model

judge: PASS if the new read use case (order detail by id) returns a ReadModel record provided by a QueryHandler, and neither this new use case nor its web endpoint returns or exposes the Order aggregate. Pre-existing methods (e.g. placeOrder returning Order) do not matter. FAIL otherwise.
cases.note: AGENTS.md overrides CQRS light with never expose aggregates
